articles.title: Main Event (Dave & Buster's) to Open New Location in Woodbury, MN
articles.summary: Dave & Buster's-owned entertainment brand Main Event is expanding with a new venue in Woodbury, Minnesota. The opening signals continued brick-and-mortar growth for the combined D&B/Main Event portfolio despite broader retail headwinds. FEC operators should monitor this expansion as Main Event competes directly for family entertainment spend in suburban markets.

articles.title: $50M EVO Entertainment Destination Clears Site in Downtown Clearwater
articles.summary: A $50 million EVO Entertainment complex is moving forward in downtown Clearwater, Florida, with the site now cleared for development. EVO is among the fastest-growing upscale FEC chains, combining bowling, cinema, gaming, and dining. The project signals strong investor confidence in large-format entertainment destinations in urban cores.

articles.title: Topgolf Launches Media Network and Licensing Division
articles.summary: Topgolf has unveiled a new media network and licensing division designed to connect brands with its 42 million annual guests in a single entry point. This move positions Topgolf as a media platform as much as a venue operator, opening new non-admission revenue streams. FEC operators should watch this model as a blueprint for monetizing large captive guest audiences.

articles.title: Round1 Bowling & Arcade Eyes FY2027 Opening for Second Maryland Location
articles.summary: Japanese entertainment giant Round1 is planning a second Maryland location with a target opening in fiscal year 2027. Round1's continued U.S. expansion underscores the strength of the multi-attraction bowling-and-arcade format in suburban and mall environments. Competing FEC operators in the mid-Atlantic region should take note of the incoming competition.

articles.title: Slick City Action Park Opens New Location in Parma, Ohio
articles.summary: Slick City Action Park, the slide-focused indoor attraction brand, has opened a new venue in Parma, Ohio. The opening continues Slick City's rapid national expansion of its distinctive slide-and-entertainment concept. The chain's growth is a notable data point for investors evaluating the indoor active-entertainment segment.

articles.title: Thrillz Atlanta Opens as Massive Indoor Adventure Park
articles.summary: Thrillz Atlanta has officially opened, offering a large-format indoor adventure park experience in the Atlanta market. The venue joins a growing wave of multi-activity indoor parks competing for family and group entertainment dollars in major metros. FEC operators can benchmark Thrillz's attraction mix and pricing strategy as the brand scales.

articles.title: Universal Reports Near-Term Softness in Theme Parks Despite Epic Universe Boost
articles.summary: Comcast reported that Universal's theme parks revenue rose 2.7% year-over-year to $2.4 billion in Q2, but adjusted EBITDA fell 5.1% due to higher operating costs. Executives flagged near-term softness in the segment even as Epic Universe drove Orlando gains. For FEC operators, this signals that even marquee attractions are not immune to consumer spending caution and cost inflation pressures.

articles.title: West Des Moines Approves Development Agreement for Grand Experience Entertainment Complex
articles.summary: West Des Moines city officials have approved a development agreement for the Grand Experience, a new large-scale entertainment destination. Municipal approvals of this nature often unlock significant private investment and can reshape local entertainment landscapes. FEC operators and developers in the Midwest should track this project as a potential competitor and market indicator.

articles.title: Paladin Midway Installs 100 Intercard Impulse Plus Readers on Mobile Game Trucks
articles.summary: Paladin Amusements has equipped 100 mobile game trucks with Intercard's new Impulse Plus kiosk-free card readers that accept both credit cards and game cards directly at the game. The deployment eliminates the need for a separate kiosk, streamlining the payment experience for guests on midway and mobile formats. FEC operators running arcade or midway games should evaluate this frictionless payment solution for improving throughput and revenue capture.

articles.title: Legends Entertainment Selects Intercard Kiosks for Springfield Arcade
articles.summary: Legends Entertainment has chosen Intercard's kiosk systems for its Springfield arcade operation, continuing Intercard's strong presence in the FEC payment and loyalty space. Cashless and card-based systems remain a top operational priority for arcade and FEC venues seeking to reduce cash handling and improve guest data capture. This deployment offers a real-world case study for operators evaluating kiosk upgrades.

articles.title: Lefty's Alley and Eats Opens in Newark, Delaware
articles.summary: Lefty's Alley and Eats, a bowling-and-dining concept, has opened a new location in Newark, Delaware. The venue represents the continued growth of the eatertainment model combining bowling lanes with a full food and beverage program. Operators in the bowling sector can watch Lefty's expansion for insights on menu integration and market positioning.

articles.title: Megaplex Entertainment Center Announced for St. George, Utah's New Paseo Complex
articles.summary: A Megaplex entertainment center is slated to anchor the new Paseo mixed-use development in St. George, Utah, alongside Nordstrom Rack. Pairing large-format entertainment with retail in mixed-use developments is an increasingly common strategy for driving foot traffic to both. FEC developers and operators should note this as a model for retail-entertainment co-tenancy deals.

articles.title: Altitude Trampoline Park to Open New Location in Litchfield Park, Arizona
articles.summary: Altitude Trampoline Park is bringing a new location to Litchfield Park in the Phoenix metro area, adding to its growing national footprint. Trampoline parks continue to expand aggressively into suburban markets, increasing competition for family entertainment visits. Operators in the active-entertainment segment should monitor Altitude's site selection strategy.

articles.title: Zamania Sportainment Venue Opens at Ibn Battuta Mall in Dubai
articles.summary: Zamania by Leo & Loona has opened a new sportainment venue at Ibn Battuta Mall in Dubai, combining active sports and entertainment in a retail anchor format. The Middle East continues to be a hotbed for new FEC and entertainment concepts, drawing interest from global operators and investors. This opening highlights the growing international appetite for mall-based active entertainment.

articles.title: Fun City Adventure Park Plans New Oklahoma City Location
articles.summary: Fun City Adventure Park is planning an expansion into Oklahoma City, signaling growing demand for indoor family adventure concepts in mid-sized U.S. markets. The brand's expansion adds to the competitive indoor entertainment landscape in the South-Central region. FEC operators and investors in Oklahoma and surrounding states should monitor the project's progress.

articles.title: 'Funflation' Trend Pushes Up Costs Across Gaming and Leisure Sectors
articles.summary: A growing consumer trend dubbed 'funflation' is driving up prices across gaming, out-of-home entertainment, and OTT platforms as operators pass rising costs to guests. For FEC operators, this trend creates both a challenge in maintaining value perception and an opportunity as consumers still prioritize experiences. Understanding funflation dynamics is critical for pricing strategy and marketing positioning in the current economic environment.

articles.title: Elevation Station Returns to Covington, Louisiana with New Location
articles.summary: Elevation Station, an indoor entertainment venue, has reopened in Covington, Louisiana at a new location after a period of absence from the market. Venue relocations can be an effective strategy for refreshing a brand and capturing new customer segments in a familiar market. FEC operators navigating lease renewals or site changes can learn from this relaunch approach.

articles.title: New Retro-Inspired Amusement Center to Open in North Charleston, SC
articles.summary: A new retro-themed amusement center is set to open in North Charleston, South Carolina, tapping into nostalgia-driven entertainment trends. Retro aesthetics have proven popular with both millennial parents and their children, offering a differentiated positioning in crowded FEC markets. Operators considering concept refreshes may find the retro approach a compelling angle for guest engagement.

articles.title: New Family Amusement Center with Restaurant and Bar Opens in Charleston, SC Area
articles.summary: A new family amusement center combining arcade-style attractions with a restaurant and full bar is opening in the Charleston, South Carolina area. The food-and-beverage integration model continues to prove its appeal as a revenue diversifier for FEC operators. This opening is a timely case study in the eatertainment format for operators considering F&B expansions.

articles.title: Dundee to Get Its First Indoor Crazy Golf Venue as Safari & Co Prepares to Open
articles.summary: Safari & Co is bringing the first indoor crazy golf concept to Dundee, Scotland, continuing the rapid spread of competitive socializing venues across UK cities. Indoor mini golf has become one of the fastest-growing FEC sub-categories in the UK and is increasingly crossing into U.S. and international markets. Operators considering adding social entertainment attractions should track this format's expansion trajectory.

articles.title: Fusion Family Fun Center Holds Grand Opening in Bremen, Indiana
articles.summary: Fusion Family Fun Center celebrated its grand opening ribbon cutting in Bremen, Indiana, bringing a new multi-activity entertainment option to the small-market community. New FEC openings in smaller markets demonstrate that the industry's growth is not limited to major metros. Operators and investors targeting secondary and tertiary markets can reference this opening as a proof point.

articles.title: Tornado Terry's FEC Shuts Down for Good After Years of Operation
articles.summary: Tornado Terry's, a family entertainment center in the Dallas-Fort Worth area, is permanently closing its doors. The closure highlights ongoing challenges for independent FEC operators competing against well-capitalized national chains. Understanding the factors behind closures like this can help operators proactively address vulnerabilities in their own business models.

articles.title: Longtime Fort Worth Arcade Closes After 35 Years
articles.summary: A beloved Fort Worth arcade is shutting down after 35 years in business, marking the end of an era for the local entertainment community. The closure underscores the mounting pressure on legacy amusement operators facing rising rents, evolving consumer tastes, and competition from modern FEC formats. Industry veterans can reflect on what long-term sustainability requires in today's entertainment landscape.

articles.title: Panasonic and Illumibot Launch AI-Powered Projection Mapping Mobile Units
articles.summary: Panasonic Projector & Display Americas has partnered with Illumibot to introduce AI-powered mobile projection mapping units that use smartphone cameras and natural language prompts to detect surfaces and generate mapped visuals. This technology could lower the barrier to immersive projection experiences for smaller FEC and entertainment venues that lack dedicated technical staff. Operators exploring immersive environment upgrades should watch this product's commercial availability.

articles.title: Dallas-Area FEC Blames Nearby Construction for Forced Closure
articles.summary: A family entertainment center in the Dallas, Texas area has closed, citing prolonged nearby construction as a primary driver of the business disruption. Construction-related access issues and reduced visibility are an underappreciated operational risk for FEC venues in developing commercial corridors. Operators in active development zones should consider lease protections and contingency planning for similar scenarios.

articles.title: Halloween Horror Nights Adds Fortnite-Themed Scare Zone at Universal Orlando and Hollywood
articles.summary: Universal Orlando and Universal Studios Hollywood are adding a Fortnitemares-inspired scare zone to Halloween Horror Nights this fall, tapping into the massive Fortnite gaming audience. The IP crossover between video gaming and live entertainment reflects a broader trend of gaming brands extending into physical experiences. FEC operators running seasonal haunted or horror events can study Universal's IP licensing approach to attract gaming-oriented demographics.

articles.title: Massanutten Resort Debuts Alpine Coaster as New Attraction
articles.summary: Virginia's Massanutten Resort has opened Mountain Mayhem, an alpine coaster stretching 2,156 feet of track with two full 360-degree spirals. Alpine and mountain coasters continue to grow as a popular add-on attraction for resorts and outdoor entertainment destinations. FEC operators with outdoor space should evaluate alpine coaster installations as a high-thrill, relatively low-staffing attraction option.

articles.title: Legoland Parks Expand Halloween with New Brick or Treat Street Experiences
articles.summary: Legoland Florida and Legoland California are rolling out Brick or Treat Street, an interactive trick-or-treating walkthrough featuring six life-sized Lego Monster homes for this year's Halloween events. The family-focused seasonal event strategy demonstrates how attractions can differentiate Halloween programming to appeal to younger children rather than compete on scare factor. FEC operators running seasonal events can borrow from Legoland's age-appropriate theming approach to broaden their Halloween audience.

articles.title: Permit Hurdles Delay New Fun Center Near Southport, NC
articles.summary: A new family fun center planned near Southport, North Carolina is facing delays due to permitting challenges with local authorities. Regulatory and permit bottlenecks are a common obstacle for new FEC developments and can significantly impact opening timelines and pre-opening marketing plans. Developers and operators in the planning stages should factor extended permitting timelines into project schedules.

articles.title: Gilroy Gardens Launches Hecker Pass Outdoor Events Center as New Revenue Stream
articles.summary: Gilroy Gardens Family Theme Park has rebranded and launched Hecker Pass Outdoor Events Center, a dedicated outdoor events venue with its own website and brand identity. The move represents a strategic diversification for the nonprofit-operated park to capture private event and corporate revenue beyond day-visit admissions. FEC operators looking to grow group and event business can study Gilroy Gardens' approach to carving out a distinct events brand.
